haiku-low.q1: If reports.row_count (unfiltered, from replica) is 10,000 or less, the CSV streams directly and the page saves it. Above 10,000, it returns 202 queued and emails a link.
haiku-low.q2: The unique index rejects the new row, so the API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status, and no new job starts.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The stored file is removed after 7 days by a bucket lifecycle rule, with no cleanup code.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, numbered 1-3, with retries after 60s and 300s. Then the row is marked failed and a failure email is sent, and the page shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.'
haiku-low.q5: The replica. Every path reads report rows only from the replica.
haiku-low.q6: Status is stored in the primary DB report_exports table. The page polls GET /api/exports/{id} every 5s, and on load calls the latest-export endpoint, so reopening shows current status.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row batches from the replica, buffers CSV up to 8 MB, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, so memory stays near one batch plus one buffer.
haiku-low.q8: Data is discarded: failures abort the multipart upload, and crashes leave an incomplete upload that is invisible and deleted after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts from row one with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: They are saved on the report_exports row at click time and stay frozen. The job payload carries only export_id, so the job reads filters and columns from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running, enforced by the database.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be completed with object_key set and a signed URL created. The job then sends the email and marks succeeded. If rerun after success or failure it returns; if object_key is set it skips to mail.
haiku-low.q12: If the replica fails mid-stream the connection drops. The page shows the export-failed message, saves nothing, and does not retry automatically.

sonnet.q1: By reports.row_count (unfiltered total, read off the replica). If 10,000 or less: sync download, API returns 200 text/csv streamed and the page saves it as a file (no job, record, or storage). If more than 10,000: background job; user gets 202 queued, then an emailed download link (24h signed URL) when done.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') rejects the insert; the API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status and starts no new job.
sonnet.q3: The signed link works 24 hours (ttl_seconds=86400). The file is removed by the bucket's rule after 7 days; there is no other cleanup.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts (numbered 1-3; retries after 60 s and 300 s). After the 3rd failure, on_final_failure sets the row to failed (with error and finished_at), then sends a report_export_failed email (if that mail fails it is only logged). The page shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.'
sonnet.q5: The replica (both the sync and background paths read report rows from the replica only).
sonnet.q6: In the status column of the report_exports row in the primary DB. The page polls GET /api/exports/{export_id} every 5 s while queued/running (stops on succeeded/failed). On reopening, it first calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest to get the user's newest export, then polls that id.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads 5,000-row batches off the replica (row_id > last ORDER BY row_id), CSV-encodes into a buffer, and uploads each 8 MB as a multipart part, leftover as last part, then complete_multipart. Worst case memory is one batch plus one 8 MB buffer; ~900 MB is about 115 parts (limit 10,000), fine under 512 MB, taking a few minutes within the 30-minute timeout.
sonnet.q8: On an exception it calls abort_multipart and re-raises; on a crash or 30-minute kill the upload never completes, so nothing is visible, and the bucket discards incomplete uploads after 24 h. The next attempt starts again from row one with a new multipart upload.
sonnet.q9: Frozen in the filters and columns fields of the report_exports row inserted at click time. The job payload contains only export_id; the worker loads the row by that id to get them.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') in the report_exports table; the loser's insert is rejected and it returns 200 with the existing export.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete (complete_multipart done and object_key written) and the signed URL generated before the mail is sent; status succeeded is set only after the mail goes out. On re-run: if status is succeeded or failed it just returns; if running with object_key already set it skips the file build and goes straight to the mail step.
sonnet.q12: Replica dies before first byte: 503. Dies mid-stream: connection is dropped. The page shows the export-failed message and saves nothing; no automatic retry.
